members.signature: public static IResourceBuilder<EntraIdApplicationResource> EntraIdResourceExtensions.AddEntraIdApplication(this IDistributedApplicationBuilder builder, string name)

summary.text: Adds a Microsoft Entra ID application registration resource to the application model.

children.text: The Entra ID application resource injects configuration as environment variables into consuming services. For .NET programs, the variables default to the
AzureAd
configuration section that Microsoft.Identity.Web reads natively.

By default, Aspire provisions an application and service principal using the Microsoft Graph Bicep extension. This requires Azure provisioning configuration and permission to create registrations in the subscription's tenant. Call
AddExistingEntraIdApplication
to reference an existing registration without Azure or Graph access.

arguments.Reason: The addExistingEntraIdApplication export accepts literal or parameter IDs independently.

summary.text: Adds a reference to an existing Microsoft Entra ID application registration without enabling Azure provisioning.

children.text: Both the tenant ID and client ID are required to identify an existing Entra ID application. Unlike ARM resources that can be identified by name and resource group, Entra ID app registrations live in a specific tenant directory and are uniquely identified by their client ID within that tenant.
The parameter values are validated when the application starts. The tenant ID must be a GUID or a domain such as
contoso.onmicrosoft.com
, and the client ID must be a GUID. When a value is missing or malformed, the resource reports
FailedToStart
and logs the reason.
The registration is used only for configuration. Aspire does not deploy Bicep or query Microsoft Graph for this resource. Use
to create a registration instead.

summary.text: When published, assigns application roles of this API to a user-assigned managed identity.

The caller authenticates directly as its managed identity; no caller registration or federated credential is created. This does not attach the identity to a workload or configure its token acquisition. The API must validate tokens and enforce the required role.

summary.text: Creates and provisions a short-lived certificate credential for local development.

children.text: Each application gets a dedicated certificate in the AppHost's local store. Certificates last two days; on a subsequent run, a certificate with one day or less remaining is replaced by overwriting its PFX file. Only the public certificate is provisioned in Entra. Referencing applications receive the private credential as a secret
Base64EncodedValue
in Microsoft.Identity.Web's
ClientCredentials
configuration. Aspire replaces the registration's entire
keyCredentials
collection with the selected certificate. Existing certificate credentials are not retained, so older sessions must restart after renewal.

Development and production must use separate Entra registrations. Never register developer certificates on a production application. Different resource groups do not isolate tenant-scoped registrations: use distinct registration names or tenant-resource suffixes. This method does not provision or emit a credential when publishing; omitting a credential from publish does not revoke a key previously registered against the same application. In either mode, this configuration prevents conversion to an existing registration with
AsExistingApplication
Renewal is checked at AppHost startup, not in the background. Restart long-running development sessions before the certificate expires. Use
PublishWithFederatedManagedIdentityCredential
for deployed workloads.

summary.text: Adds redirect URIs for a resource's endpoint to a registration created by Aspire.

children.text: In run mode the origin comes from the endpoint's finalized browser URLs, including vanity hostnames and URL customization. When publishing or deploying, the origin comes from the resource's compute environment, and the deployed endpoint must have TLS enabled. After endpoint allocation, resolution waits up to 30 seconds for finalized browser URLs. If they are not ready, the allocated origin is used with a warning. Supply explicit redirect URIs if that address differs from the browser URL.

The callback path can't be discovered from the endpoint: it's configured by the consuming application, so it is supplied here and must match that configuration. When the externally visible URL differs from the endpoint (gateway, reverse proxy, or custom domain), supply the full URL with
WithRedirectUris
instead. Throws for existing registrations; configure their redirect URIs manually.

Run-mode resolution waits for all URL customization callbacks to complete and uses the shared browser-origin preference order. Navigation paths are excluded before appending the supplied callback path. If URL customization removes all browser URLs for the endpoint, resolution reports a missing origin.

callbackPaths.text: The callback paths on that endpoint, such as

endpoint.text: The endpoint that serves the callbacks.

A permission, identified by name and optionally by ID, that an application requests from an API.

remarks.text: Delegated permissions are scopes that the API exposes and the application uses on behalf of a signed-in user. Application permissions are app roles that the API defines and the application uses as itself. They are different permissions, even when they share a name, and each needs its own consent. For a permission that isn't in an API's built-in list, Aspire can't check that the name and the ID belong together. The declaration uses the ID, while a delegated consent grant names the permission, so a name that doesn't match the ID would grant a permission that was never declared. Take both from the API's service principal.

A resource that represents a Microsoft Entra ID application registration.

children.text: Entra ID application registrations define the identity configuration for services in a distributed application. Each application registration includes a tenant ID, client ID, and optionally client credentials and API scopes.
Aspire creates new registrations using a resource-group-scoped Microsoft Graph Bicep deployment. Use
AddExistingEntraIdApplication
to reference an existing registration without deploying infrastructure. Registration-only builder APIs throw on existing references. Converting a resource with
AsExistingApplication
also throws if registration-only configuration was already applied. Consumer configuration and explicit metadata describing existing API URIs and scopes remain supported.
References to this resource inject configuration as environment variables. .NET program references default to names such as
AzureAd__TenantId
and
AzureAd__ClientId
, compatible with Microsoft.Identity.Web. Other references default to an uppercase resource-name prefix and a single underscore separator, and can configure their own prefix and separator.
The properties align with
MicrosoftEntraApplicationOptions
from
Microsoft.Identity.Abstractions
